messages:
emma_sales: Quick sync — SPARK wants 30% reseller margin on our hosted API plus a 12-month commit. They want a POC-first model (3 customers) with credits and then conversion to a committed ARR. Can we do 30%? What approvals do we need? 

raj_partner: They pushed hard on margin during partner meeting. Typical is 20-25% for tier-1 resellers. 30% is high unless we get a firm revenue commit or co-selling uplift. POC -> conversion path makes sense. 

luke_finance: 30% is outside standard rate card. Our baseline reseller margin bands: Partner Bronze 15%, Silver 20%, Gold 25%. Above 25% requires deal-desk + VP approval. Need ARR commit and expected gross margin impact. Share example numbers (ARR, regions, model mix). 

emma_sales: Example: POC to convert ~3 customers, expected ARR $220k first-year run-rate if conversion succeeds. They want credits equal to 3 months of service during POC. 

luke_finance: Put that into a quick calc. 220k ARR with 30% margin = $66k partner payout; at 25% it's $55k. We need to see net revenue after discounts, plus any onboarding credit. If you can commit to a minimum 200k ARR for 12 months we can consider a one-time onboarding credit instead of 30% ongoing. 

noah_solutions: For POC ops: we can provide 3 x 2-week sandbox instances, limited tokens, and a technical onboarding session. We can't grant production keys for free. Make sure they sign the POC SOW and a temporary DPA addendum. 

anita_legal: We need: signed reseller addendum (modified MSA), completed security questionnaire, SOC2 attestation, and confirmation of customer data flows. If they want elevated margin tied to commit, legal needs the revenue guarantee clause and a clawback for churn within 6 months. 

maya_gtm: Quick product-market note: if SPARK will bring enterprise logos, treat as strategic partner; could justify higher margin but requires concrete mutual KPIs (logo count, pipeline ops). 

emma_sales: Ok — next steps I propose: 1) send finance the ARR calc spreadsheet, 2) have partner sign POC SOW + DPA, 3) run security questionnaire, 4) if ARR >= 200k then ask deal-desk for exceptional margin approval (VP sign-off). 

luke_finance: Sounds good. To expedite: drop the ARR calc and target customer list here or in a secure sheet. Deal-desk process: submit 'partner-exception' in Zendesk with list, revenue model, gross margin impact, and proposed clawback terms. I can fast-track if it's >200k and legal signs off. 

raj_partner: One more ask from SPARK — they want a co-marketing fund (MDF) of 5% of first-year ARR if we give elevated margin. How do we handle MDF? 

luke_finance: MDF is negotiable as a separate bucket. If we give an elevated margin, we typically offset with a 2-4% MDF cap and require co-op marketing plan and quarterly reporting. Anything above that needs CFO sign-off. 

anita_legal: Also confirm IP and trademark usage in the co-marketing clause. And ensure the MDF is earned upon verified pipeline activity, not just invoice. 

emma_sales: I'll collect the ARR calc, the customer list, and send the security questionnaire link to SPARK today. 

noah_solutions: I'll prep the POC SOW template and a short ops runbook for the trial. 

maya_gtm: I'll map KPIs for co-selling and draft the co-marketing plan template. 

luke_finance: Once you drop the Zendesk request, cc me and @vp_revenue for a quick decision. If everything checks out we can approve a temporary 27% margin with a 6-month review (instead of straight 30%). 

raj_partner: Great. SPARK is happy to accept 27% if onboarding credits are limited to 1 month and we get a hard commit. 

emma_sales: Sweet. I'll update SPARK and aim to file with deal-desk today. :thumbsup: 

maya_gtm: +1 :rocket:

anita_legal: adding doc checklist: reseller addendum, executed POC SOW, completed SecQ, SOC2 cert, DPA addendum. Please upload to the legal folder and tag me. 

emma_sales: Will do — thread closed after filing. Thanks team!
